newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: POLL-Brokers see Colombo stocks up 15 pct yr end.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Brokers see Colombo stocks up 15 pct yr end.

text.p: Sri Lanka's stock market will continue its current uptrend, gaining almost another 15 percent by the end of the year, a Reuters poll of local stock brokers suggested on Thursday.

Seven leading brokers forecast the benchmark Colombo Stock Exchange All Share Index would average 878.6 points by the end of September, and around 937.1 by the end of the year, from its closing position at 817.5 on Thursday.
Forecasts for the position of the index at the end of the year ranged from 850 points to 1,200 points, with five of the seven brokers predicting a range between 900 and 950.
None of the brokers predicted the index would fall from its current position or remain flat during the rest of 1997.

Dealers said the bullish outlook was due to recent political stability in the Indian Ocean island, the expectation of handsome second quarter corporate results, due out over the next few weeks, and the government's privatisation programme.
The All Share Index has already risen 35 percent this year from 607 on January 2.

But brokers said this rise was really only a recovery after a disastrous performance in 1996, when the monsoons failed and drought led to widespread power cuts across industry and a sharp decline in agricultural output.

The index is still nowhere near its peak of 1,378 points, reached in March 1994, and average price earnings ratios are now between 12 and 15 times, way below their historic high around 30 times, brokers said.
